Definition: from G2095 and G5424; to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice:--fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice.
BiblicalUsage: euphraínō means fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice. In Luke 12:19, the text says "thou hast much goods laid up for many years." In Acts 2:26, the text says "Therefore did my heart rejoice."
TheologicalSignificance: euphraínō convinces me that fellowship is sharing life together under Christ, not just sharing a room. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
